metadata.description: Node-only suites: none of them serves apps/ui/build (ui-build-snapshot.test.ts builds a fixture tree in a temp directory), so this target builds no web UI variant and carries no env fixture. serve-ui-build.test.ts reads apps/ui/serve/build, which the ui:build:serve dependency produces and caches. The browser tiers below still build ui themselves.

external-agent.spec.ts starts a real `tau serve` daemon (startTauServeFixture), which serves apps/ui/serve/build, so this target depends on ui:build:serve as test:e2e:daemon-host does; that variant needs none of the fixture below. Every ui:build consumer here builds it as its first command, under the env fixture below, instead of through dependsOn: a dependency task inherits only the caller's environment, so it could not carry the fixture. The fixture is the non-secret local URLs ci.yml sets workflow-wide plus the self-host TAU_CLOUD_ENABLED, so a clean checkout builds with no untracked apps/ui/.env; the tier's own server sets its runtime origins. ui:build declares each of these as an env input, so the self-host and the cloud (desktop-e2e, test:e2e:live) variants never share a cache entry, and building immediately before the specs means the variant in apps/ui/build is always this target's own (desktop-e2e:test:e2e, which writes the cloud variant there, runs with parallelism false). Arguments reach only the vitest command, so `--shard=<index>/<count>` selects a slice of the suite; `shards` is how many slices e2e-nightly.yml runs as separate jobs, since the whole suite outlasts one job (run 43217741985 reached 23 of its 117 files in 120 min). FL4: each configuration runs the suite with every target opened in one named flag state (TAU_E2E_FLAG_STATE, src/support/flag-state.ts); it repeats the whole env fixture because a configuration's env replaces the options' env, and the flag state is not a ui:build input because the page seeds it at runtime, so all four share one build.

TAU-UI-6: serves one ui:build as two deploys and checks that a page whose lazy chunks the newer deploy no longer serves reloads into it instead of reaching the error page. Drives Playwright's Chromium from Node; set TAU_E2E_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE to use another installed Chromium.

metadata.description: Opt-in live provider tier: the two specs that spend real provider credit and then assert the billing receipts they produced. The UI is built by the first command rather than a dependsOn, because it must be the cloud variant (TAU_CLOUD_ENABLED=true is a build-time input of ui:build) and a dependency task inherits only the caller's environment — a self-host bundle's transport omits fundedOperations entirely, so no receipt could exist to assert. global-setup.ts starts the UI only: the tier needs a cloud API already listening at TAU_E2E_API_URL (default :4000) with TAU_CLOUD_ENABLED=true, the BILLING_* secrets and the placeholder STRIPE_* values apps/api/.env.example names — nothing on the funded path calls Stripe. Also needs `pnpm infra:up` and one `pnpm db:migrate` per database fork.

Cloud-build load tier (lane A0.11): the loading rows a self-host build cannot show, because it has no billing fence and asks for /v1/projects only for a project on the Tau remote (N1, H7, N2, H6 and the U1 session discriminator). Like test:e2e:live, the first command builds the cloud UI variant (TAU_CLOUD_ENABLED=true is a build-time input of ui:build) and global-setup.ts starts the UI only. No API runs and no secret is needed: src/support/cloud-stand-ins.ts answers get-session, /v1/projects and /v1/agents by interception for a signed-in stand-in owner with one Tau-remote project, and holds an answer when a row forces its defect. TAU_BILLING_ENVIRONMENT gives the billing fence an identity to gate on. TAU_E2E_CLOUD_LOAD=true runs the cloud-only blocks of the two specs, which every other tier skips, and the name pattern (cloud-load-gate.spec.ts's block, home-load-gate.spec.ts's N1 and H7 cases) keeps home-load-gate.spec.ts's self-host cases out of this tier. Its rows pin known defects (cloudDefectRow): each is a plain test that passes while its defect assertion fails, records that failure as a notice annotation naming the defect, and fails if the assertion passes (the defect no longer reproduces: flip expectedFailure) or anything else faults. The verbose and github-actions reporters print each standing defect's notice (locally under the row, and as a workflow annotation in CI). --retry 0: a row runs once, so a sampled pass is never retried into a reading. Arguments reach only the vitest command. Its own PORT keeps it from reusing a self-host server another e2e target started.

commands: ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --project chromium --retry 0 --reporter=verbose --reporter=github-actions --testNamePattern "cloud-build tier|^N1: |^H7: " src/cloud-load-gate.spec.ts src/home-load-gate.spec.ts

metadata.description: Opt-in live GitHub tier: the C10 and A4 rows, which sign in to github.com as the two test identities (`src/support/github-identity.ts`). Like test:e2e:live, the first command builds the cloud UI variant and global-setup.ts starts the UI only: the rows need a cloud API at TAU_E2E_API_URL (default :4000) whose TAU_FRONTEND_URL is this target's origin, http://localhost:3018, with the GitHub App and GitHub sign-in configured. The API must listen on localhost:4000, because the development App's and OAuth App's registered callbacks are there. TAU_E2E_LIVE_GITHUB=true is left to the caller that started that API (e2e-nightly.yml's live-github job), so without it, or without an identity's variables, each row skips and names what is missing. --retry 0: a retry repeats a password sign-in to github.com from the same runner, and repeated sign-ins risk GitHub locking the test account.
Qualify hover, selection, list labels and source edits on the serial browser path; the existing picovoxel-multi spec owns browser pthread and cross-origin-isolation qualification.

PicoGK as a clean browser consumer: the built app serving the staged package bundle, opening the shipped C# examples through the ordinary project route. PICOGK_BROWSER_ASSETS_ROOT must name a prepared bundle, which ui:build declares as an input, so this target never reuses a build made against another bundle. Its own PORT keeps it from reusing a server another e2e target started.

Filesystem capability charter W0: the S1–S20 scenario harness on real OPFS in Playwright's Chromium, with no UI server. Writes one timing + count row per scenario (fixture, browser, server and network named) to out/test-results/filesystem-scenarios and asserts the count gates against src/filesystem-scenarios/baseline/known-red.json. The default is the small (1/20) fixture (vitest.config.ts's default; an options-level env would override the full configuration's); the full configuration is the STO-25 shape. TAU_FS_SCENARIO_RUNS sets samples per scenario, TAU_FS_SCENARIO_RECORD=true rewrites the committed baseline without loosening a known-red gate (force records the observed values as they are), TAU_FS_SCENARIO_ENGINES adds firefox/webkit where installed, and TAU_E2E_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE points at another Chromium.
